newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany teams with France on securities checks.
newsitem.headline: Germany teams with France on securities checks.

text.p: Germany's fledgling securities industry watchdog on Tuesday said it had signed an agreement to swap information with French bourse authorities.

The agreement between the Federal Securities Trading Authority, or BAWe, and the COB of France is the first of its kind since the German agency started operations in 1995 as part of the nation's crackdown on abuses in the securities industry.
"This agreement will serve to expand our close and trusting co-operation," said BAWe President Georg Wittich, who signed the deal on Tuesday with COB president Michel Prada.

Under the terms of the agreement, French and German authorities will from now on be able to commission each other to carry out investigations, using firm new guidelines on procedure and clearer communication channels.
The BAWe said the co-operation would lead to better integration on the markets and improved investor protection.
"In this sense it contributes to the realisation of the single market for securities and derivatives in Europe," the BAWe said.
The BAWe is responsible for monitoring all securities transactions in Germany and for carrying out investigations where there is a suspicion of irregularity, such as insider trading.
Investigations which yield strong evidence of wrongdoing are passed to public prosecutors.
The BAWe is also responsible for ensuring that banks and brokerages follow compliance guidelines and that companies fulfil their obligations when reporting market-sensitive news.
